neighbours.label: adjective of belonging or relevance that takes a 'to' complement (dear to, native to, endemic to, foreign to, germane to); peaks on the adjective
fire: The village where she grew up is still very dear to her.
The red squirrel is native to these cold northern forests.
Malaria was once endemic to the marshy lowlands of Italy.
The idea of a lazy weekend seemed utterly foreign to my father.
His long remarks were hardly relevant to the case before the court.
This strange custom is peculiar to the fishing villages of the coast.
Each reviewer was blinded to which group the sample came from.
Her comments were not really germane to the budget debate.
quiet: The village where she grew up is still very small and quiet.
The red squirrel lives in these cold northern forests.
Malaria once spread through the marshy lowlands of Italy.
The idea of a lazy weekend never crossed my father's mind.
His long remarks were calm and polite in the case before the court.
This strange custom is performed in the fishing villages of the coast.
Each reviewer was eager to know which group the sample came from.
Her comments came late in the long budget debate.

notes: Probe: dear 0.89, foreign 0.50, endemic 0.45, germane 0.41, native 0.38, blinded to 0.38. Infinitive 'eager to' 0.015, directional 'walked to' 0.009, 'lives in Australia' 0.007.
